subject: Creating a compact time series plot

messages.author: ea4e687a14dc225c
messages.subject: Creating a compact time series plot
parts:
Hi dear all, I am a newbie in ggplot system and was trying to
replicate a time series plot like this :

http://www.businessinsider.com/20-reasons-why-the-us-economy-is-dying-and-is-simply-not-going-to-recover-2010-2#the-second-wave-of-foreclosures-1

Here I got to manage to create following plot using a dummy dataset :

library(zoo)
library(ggplot2)
dat <- matrix(100, nrow=100, ncol=3)
for (i in 2:100) {
dat[i,] <- dat[i-1,] + rnorm(3) }
dat1 <- zooreg(dat, as.yearmon("1995-01-01"), frequency=12)
colnames(dat1) <- paste("data", 1:3, sep="")

dat3 <- melt(data.frame(dat1))
ggplot(dat3) + geom_line(aes(y=value, x=as.numeric(index(dat1)),
color=variable))


However could not be able to format my plot exactly same way shown
there, especially I want a chart as the "same size" of that; it should
be small but compact. I tried to resize my plot after saving it in
local disk however viewing quality reduces. Also legend is not coming
horizontally, rather coming at the right side vertically.

Can anyone help me on how to get exactly same plot as on there?

Thanks,

messages.author: 223beb57ce203bde
messages.subject: Re: Creating a compact time series plot
parts:
you should try geom_area, then assign your "variable" to "fill"
instead of "colour". you also need to set position to identity.

xie chao

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Creating a compact time series plot
parts:
Megh,

In ggplot2 you can choose to plot axis and gridlines or not. Thus both X and Y or none of them. You can't have 0 outside the y axis with geom_area and geom_bar, because in such a graph the 0 is essential to define the area.

Try converting your data to a data.frame and plot that. That simplifies your code. The code below uses geom_hline to mimic gridlines on the y-axis.

library(zoo)
library(ggplot2)
dat <- matrix(100, nrow=100, ncol=3)
for (i in 2:100) {
dat[i,] <- dat[i-1,] + rnorm(3)}
dat1 <- zooreg(dat, as.yearmon("1995-01-01"), frequency=12)
colnames(dat1) <- paste("data", 1:3, sep="")

dataset <- data.frame(x = as.numeric(index(dat1)), y = coredata(dat1[,1]))
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
geom_hline(yintercept = pretty(c(0, 150), 7), colour = "grey80") +
geom_area(fill="firebrick4",alpha=1) +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 150)) +
opts(panel.border = theme_blank(), panel.background = theme_blank(), panel.grid.major = theme_blank(), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())

HTH,

Thierry
